Nine former FBI employees are suing the bureau
and Director Cash Patel over what they say
was their unlawful firing for having worked
on an investigation into President Trump.
The lawsuit says the former FBI agents, analysts,
and specialists were targets of political retribution,
NPR's Ryan Lucas has more.
The lawsuit says the nine former FBI employees
were members of elite counterintelligence
and intelligence squads,

They were all assigned to work on the investigation
into President Trump's alleged mishandling
of classified documents after his first term in office.
The lawsuit says they were all fired in February,
quote, "not for any cause or legitimate reason,
but only to satisfy the president's personal vendetta,"
end quote.
It says the firings violated their first
and fifth amendment rights,
they are seeking to be reinstated in their jobs at the FBI,
and any back pay, they would be due.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky

after the US placed restrictions on Starlink systems

Trump also recently made a deal to import Russian diesel fuel
despite international efforts to sanction Russia.

Retail spending rose by 8/10 of a percent last month.
Much of this was at the pump.
Gas station spending alone jumped by 6.4%,
spending at grocery stores and restaurants also rose slightly.
These numbers don't necessarily mean
Americans are buying more.
Inflation is driving up the cost of most goods.
The data does indicate, however,
that consumers are resilient.
Some analysts stress that while the economy

Rooney says she's been honest about her beliefs
